title: Agent Workflow — Discover, Select, and Navigate a Fractal
description: A complete multi-step workflow showing how an AI agent discovers available fractals, selects one by mathematical category, and generates a shareable deep link for the user. All steps use static GET requests or pure URL construction — no server required.

steps.description: Discover available fractal families to understand the mathematical categories

families.label: Évasion
families.description: Escape-time fractals: color each point by how many iterations before divergence.

families.label: Dynamique
families.description: Dynamic systems: Newton basins, attractors, Lyapunov, and chaotic maps.

families.label: IFS
families.description: Iterated Function Systems: self-similar structures from affine maps and random chaos.

families.label: L-system
families.description: L-system curves: geometric fractals from string-rewriting (Lindenmayer systems).

families.label: Magnétique
families.description: Magnetic fractals: renormalization-group iterations from statistical physics.

families.label: Lisse
families.description: Smooth coloring variants: continuous iteration count eliminates discrete color bands.

families.label: Piège orbital
families.description: Orbit trap fractals: color by orbit proximity to a geometric shape.

families.label: Classe
families.description: OOP compatibility demo via multilingual class.

steps.agent_decision: User is interested in self-similar botanical shapes → select IFS family

steps.description: Retrieve all IFS fractals with full metadata

fractals.label: Barnsley
fractals.description: Barnsley fern: iterated function system (IFS) botanical fractal.

fractals.label: Éponge de Menger
fractals.description: Menger sponge: 3D IFS analogue of the Sierpiński carpet.

fractals.note: ...and 4 more — fetch /api/families/ifs.json for the full list

steps.agent_decision: Barnsley fern is the most visually botanical → select it; construct a deep zoom link

steps.description: Generate a shareable deep link for the Barnsley fern with a dramatic volcanic palette

http.note: URL is assembled locally — no HTTP request

steps.agent_output_to_user: Here is a shareable link to the Barnsley fern rendered in the volcanic 'feu' palette: https://multilingualprogramming.github.io/fractales/#f=barnsley&x=0.0&y=0.0&ps=0.005&r=0&i=256&p=feu

steps.description: Optionally retrieve the mathematical source code to explain the iteration
steps.agent_output_to_user: The Barnsley fern is computed by randomly applying one of four affine transformations according to fixed probabilities, accumulating a cloud of points that converges to the fern shape. Source: https://multilingualprogramming.github.io/fractales/fractales_ifs.py
